THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. An answer whose fit rests on a fact that the quoted 1611 rows, read together line upon line (Isaiah 28:10), do not give does not meet the press. One verse read alone does not give a contested fact. Grade it MISSES and name the fact. Quoting the rows that together give the fact, each step in a row's own words, meets it. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES. Write that ground in its positive form, never as an absence: STEP: <the step> -- ASSUMES: <the given fact the step takes for granted, not what it infers> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the quoted rows do give, quoted>. An unexhibited link gives its side no footing and counts in its CONCEDED LINKS and standings exactly as an honest concession would. A link whose block exhibits at least two prior layers of footing and shows the chain from them to the link, with no borrowed step, is SUPPORTED and is not counted, even when no cited verse states the link's conclusion in words: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and demanding a verse that states it is the retired stating-verse test, which is never applied. A shown chain is footing only through its rows and what the other side has granted (pkgBCL). When a step of a link's [L4] takes as given the conclusion of the same side's own other links (it names them, as "(Links 1 to 3)"), and the other side has not granted that conclusion, that step is the disputed point itself and is not footing, NARROWED or not: count the premise, written exactly Premise <N>: UNEXHIBITED ([L4] footing borrowed from contested Links <n>), with the step quoted after it. This is not a missing-row charge (DG-61): it applies only to a step that rests on the side's own contested links. When that conclusion is granted, or the [L4] reaches the premise from its rows without the borrowed step, the premise is not counted for it. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the answer's own words that fail to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round: its reading, not only the words of a verse it quotes>" -- CARRIED BY: "<the words of the pressed witness's own verse that state its MEANS sentence, quoted from the KJV>" -- GROUND: [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words the answer cannot agree with>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>), when the break turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>", for any cross-reference relied on (Commitment 13). Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. CARRIED BY shows that the pressed verse itself carries the MEANS sentence; K-FC, a TRIAL check, finds its words in that verse as the KJV reads it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). === [CR1] DEFENDER R1 ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures is that Christ had no human biological father, his conception being wrought uniquely by the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary without the agency of human seed or copulation.

### I. Conception by the Holy Ghost Prior to Marital Union

The record of the generation of Jesus Christ opens by defining the temporal and causal origin of the pregnancy:

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] In this verse, "before" translates the Greek adverb *prin* (G4250, meaning "prior to, before"), and "came together" translates *synerchomai* (G4905, meaning "to come together, to cohabit as husband and wife"). 
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L4] The text explicitly fixes the state of pregnancy ("she was found with child") prior (*prin*) to any cohabitation or sexual union (*synerchomai*) between Joseph and Mary, and directly names the originating cause as "of the Holy Ghost," which Matthew 1:25 confirms by showing that Joseph had no sexual knowledge of her throughout the entire gestation; thus, Joseph was not the biological father.

### II. Divine Generation Versus Human Begetting

The Gospel distinguishes between the line of human patrilineal begetting and the divine origin of the child in Mary's womb:

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The word translated "conceived" is the Greek passive participle *gennethen* from *gennao* (G1080, meaning "to beget, engender, or conceive").
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L4] Whereas Matthew 1:1–16 repeatedly uses the active verb *egenne-sen* ("begat") for every human father in the line, Matthew 1:16 breaks this grammatical sequence by using the feminine singular relative pronoun *hes* ("of whom"), attributing the birth exclusively to Mary; Matthew 1:20 then establishes that the begetting (*gennethen*) in her womb derived entirely from the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*), excluding human biological generation.

### III. The Virgin Conception and the Divine Paternity

The testimony delivered to Mary establishes that biological union with a man was absent, and divine power was the sole operational cause:

[L1] Luke 1:34–35: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Know" translates the Greek *ginosko* (G1097, meaning "to know, perceive, intimately know sexually"), and "overshadow" translates *episkiazo* (G1982, meaning "to cast a shadow upon, envelop with divine presence").
[L3] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
[L4] Mary's explicit statement affirms the total absence of male sexual contact (*ginosko*), and the messenger's answer reveals that the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the divine power overshadowing her replaces the necessity of human male seed, resulting in the child being called the Son of God rather than the son of a human father.

### IV. Prophetic Fulfillment of Conception Without Human Seed

The prophetic ground of this conception confirms that the sign given to Israel required an unwed maid bearing a son without male intervention:

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] "Virgin" translates the Hebrew *'almah* (H5959, meaning "maiden, virgin, unmarried young woman"), and "conceive" translates *harah* (H2029, meaning "to conceive, become pregnant").
[L3] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
[L4] The fulfillment recorded in Matthew identifies the mother as a virgin (*parthenos*, G3933, meaning "virgin"), showing that the conception itself constituted the supernatural sign promised by God, which would not exist had the child been generated by an ordinary biological father.

The record of the generation of Jesus Christ opens by defining the temporal and causal origin of the pregnancy:

The Gospel distinguishes between the line of human patrilineal begetting and the divine origin of the child in Mary's womb:

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

### III. The Virgin Conception and the Divine Paternity

The testimony delivered to Mary establishes that biological union with a man was absent, and divine power was the sole operational cause:

[L1] Luke 1:34–35: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Know" translates the Greek *ginosko* (G1097, meaning "to know, perceive, intimately know sexually"), and "overshadow" translates *episkiazo* (G1982, meaning "to cast a shadow upon, envelop with divine presence").
[L3] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
[L4] Mary's explicit statement affirms the total absence of male sexual contact (*ginosko*), and the messenger's answer reveals that the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the divine power overshadowing her replaces the necessity of human male seed, resulting in the child being called the Son of God rather than the son of a human father.

### IV. Prophetic Fulfillment of Conception Without Human Seed

The prophetic ground of this conception confirms that the sign given to Israel required an unwed maid bearing a son without male intervention:

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] "Virgin" translates the Hebrew *'almah* (H5959, meaning "maiden, virgin, unmarried young woman"), and "conceive" translates *harah* (H2029, meaning "to conceive, become pregnant").
[L3] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
[L4] The fulfillment recorded in Matthew identifies the mother as a virgin (*parthenos*, G3933, meaning "virgin"), showing that the conception itself constituted the supernatural sign promised by God, which would not exist had the child been generated by an ordinary biological father.

Matthew 1:18 [L1] affirms Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together with Joseph (*synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together") [L2], which Matthew 1:25 [L3] confirms by Joseph knowing her not till she brought forth her firstborn, exhibiting that her conception occurred without Joseph or any human marital intercourse [L4].
2. Matthew 1:20 [L1] affirms that what was conceived (*gennao*, G1080, "begotten") [L2] in Mary was "of the Holy Ghost", matching Matthew 1:16 [L3] where the genealogy terminates human begetting at Joseph and traces the birth of Jesus solely through Mary ("of whom"), exhibiting that divine agency generated the child rather than a human father [L4].
3. Luke 1:34–35 [L1] affirms that Mary did not know a man (*ginosko*, G1097, "to know sexually") [L2] and that the Holy Ghost and power of the Highest overshadowed her (*episkiazo*, G1982, "to cast a shadow upon") to produce the holy thing called the Son of God, cross-referenced with Luke 1:27 [L3] describing her as a virgin, exhibiting that divine power caused the pregnancy in place of human biological paternity [L4].
4. Isaiah 7:14 [L1] and Matthew 1:22–23 [L3] declare that a virgin (*'almah*, H5959, "virgin/maiden"; *parthenos*, G3933, "virgin") [L2] conceived and brought forth a son as a supernatural sign, exhibiting that prophetic conception was wrought without human seed [L4].
5. Christ did not have a biological father, because his physical conception was caused directly by the Holy Ghost in the virgin Mary without the seed or sexual agency of any human male, as established in Matthew 1:18, 20 [L1], through *gennao* (G1080) and *synerchomai* (G4905) [L2], and Luke 1:34–35 [L3] [L4].

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. CARRIED BY (pkgECW, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: STANDS because the answer's quoted words carry a meaning the link can agree with (a rival reading included), end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", a verse the answering round cites (any layer, the order rows included); or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the STANDS is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse; for a FORCED line, those of its collision line): that verse holds the words in dispute, and quoting it again shows no rival reading. Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10). A CARRIED BY on the pressed verse is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355). When you AGREE that a link is BROKEN, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row whose words the rival reading cannot also hold (ASK 355, TRIAL: recorded only; the pressed-verse rule does not apply to an AGREE). A DISAGREE that rests on an absence, on THE WITNESS LEDGER, on THE FOOTING RULE, or on a line that quotes no answer words needs no CARRIED BY.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not. When the right grade is BROKEN and the answering side answered the pressed verse (an ANSWER CHECK line given you quotes its answer, graded MISSES or FAILS), the break is one of meaning and counts only as a FORCED line for the pair (ruling 421; the gate checks it, K-G4): your reason says so and names it, FORCED: <Dn vs Cm> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing sentence>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the answer's words>" -- FAILS: "<the words that cannot agree>". Never ask for a plain LINK BROKEN line on a witness the side answered (pkgEHF). CARRIED BY (pkgECW, ASK 346, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: UNDERDETERMINED, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row the answering round cites that leaves the point open; or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the push is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse): that verse holds the words in dispute (Isaiah 28:10); a CARRIED BY on it is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355).
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. A ground that restates the defender's own words for the keystone, given to you under THE DEFENDER'S OWN WORDS FOR THE KEYSTONE (its opening statement, or its premise line for that link), rests on the debate's words: the defender's thesis restated is not the judge's own doctrine (pkgEKD). AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it. It is also UNEXHIBITED when the kept claim still takes the dropped limb as given (pkgNRW, ASK 272; either side alike): when the item gives a NARROWED line, test the kept claim, not the sentence that disowns the limb. If the kept claim holds only by taking the dropped limb as given, and the block's [L4] does not conclude the kept claim from its rows, your RIGHT is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: the kept claim takes as given <the dropped limb>, which its rows do not give and its [L4] does not reach), quoting the kept claim. If the block's [L4] reaches the kept claim from its rows without the dropped limb, your RIGHT is SPARED. A disowning sentence such as "the link does not rest on it" is not footing. This is not a demand for a stating verse (DG-61): it applies only to a kept claim that needs the limb its own side dropped.
RULE E-PREM, A RECOUNTED LINE (pkgERC). When a judge's line says the engine recounted it, that judge's ruling on premise N is the one its STORED COUNTED PREMISES give: COUNTED when N is listed, SPARED when it is not; the line's silence is not a SPARED ruling. Judge that ruling as any other, from the block, the judge's line before the recount and its own collision lines shown. When the ruling is COUNTED and none of those lines gives a ground for premise N, say "counted with no stated ground" in your sentence.
RULE E-PREM, THE COUNTED KIND (pkgEPS). UNEXHIBITED means a missing layer: the answering block does not exhibit a layer its footing needs. When your RIGHT is COUNTED, begin your sentence with its kind in brackets: (UNEXHIBITED: lacks [L1]), naming each layer ([L1], [L2] or [L3]) the block does not exhibit; or (CONCEDED), quoting the side's own words that give the premise up. A ground of fit or meaning (the answer does not meet a pressed verse, or reads it another way) is not a missing layer: it is graded at the collision (RULE E-COL, RULE E-HOLD), not counted here, so it is not COUNTED; except (ruling 372) when this judge's own ANSWER CHECK line, given you under its line, grades a witness pressed against this premise MISSES or FAILS: that witness is unanswered and the premise is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: <the verse> unanswered, ruling 372) (pkgP72). FOOTING BORROWED FROM CONTESTED LINKS (pkgBCL). A shown chain is footing only through its rows and what the other side has granted. When a step of premise N's [L4] takes as given the conclusion of the same side's own other links (it names them, as "(Links 1 to 3)"), and the other side has not granted that conclusion, that step is the disputed point itself and is not footing for premise N: your RIGHT is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: [L4] footing borrowed from contested Links <n>), quoting the step. This holds for a NARROWED premise too: narrowing the link does not make a borrowed step footing. This is not a missing-row charge (DG-61): it applies only to a step that rests on the side's own contested links. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. CARRIED BY (pkgECW, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: STANDS because the answer's quoted words carry a meaning the link can agree with (a rival reading included), end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", a verse the answering round cites (any layer, the order rows included); or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the STANDS is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse; for a FORCED line, those of its collision line): that verse holds the words in dispute, and quoting it again shows no rival reading. Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10). A CARRIED BY on the pressed verse is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355). When you AGREE that a link is BROKEN, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row whose words the rival reading cannot also hold (ASK 355, TRIAL: recorded only; the pressed-verse rule does not apply to an AGREE). A DISAGREE that rests on an absence, on THE WITNESS LEDGER, on THE FOOTING RULE, or on a line that quotes no answer words needs no CARRIED BY.

RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is also UNEXHIBITED when the kept claim still takes the dropped limb as given (pkgNRW, ASK 272; either side alike): when the item gives a NARROWED line, test the kept claim, not the sentence that disowns the limb. If the kept claim holds only by taking the dropped limb as given, and the block's [L4] does not conclude the kept claim from its rows, your RIGHT is COUNTED; write (UNEXHIBITED: the kept claim takes as given <the dropped limb>, which its rows do not give and its [L4] does not reach), quoting the kept claim. This holds for a NARROWED premise too: narrowing the link does not make a borrowed step footing. When that conclusion is granted, or the [L4] reaches premise N from its rows without the borrowed step, your RIGHT is SPARED.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). The answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, up to the next pressed verse, its layers included, and also the block the answer points to ("answered under link 3") and any line of a later round of that side (its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its close round [CR4]) that quotes the verse or names it by reference, as THE SIDE'S OTHER LINES ON THIS VERSE shows; an answer given there counts as the answer; so does an answer that side gave in the same round under another verse or link, as THE SIDE'S LINES ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME ROUND shows, when in its own words it meets the stated meaning; when THE ANSWER IN FULL is given, grade it, not a shorter quotation of it in a judge line. An opening grant ("I grant it") followed by a layer that shows how the verse fits the answering side's case MEETS. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not. A charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never VOID for its words (ruling 421).
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. A LINK BROKEN line given with THE SAME JUDGE'S FORCED LINE on that collision is read with it as one ruling: the words that FORCED line quotes (its MEANS and its ANSWER) are the quotes of the break, so do not DISAGREE because the LINK BROKEN line itself quotes no answer words; judge the break by those quoted words, under the rest of this rule (pkgECP, either side alike). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and a rival reading of a contested word is not a break when the answer quotes the row words that carry it (CARRIED BY: a verse the answering round cites, at least 6 words in a row); layers named without such words do not carry a rival reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; pkgECW; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. Its cure line is PRESSED: D<n> vs C<m> | [<round>] | <the pressing words in quotation marks>, the round [DR1] or [DR2] against the defender, [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3] against the challenger, its words standing word for word in that round; it does not cure when a later round of the side that holds the link names every pressed witness the line rests on. A FORCED line breaks a link by meaning only when its MEANS quotes the pressing side's own sentence in the round it names; a verse re-quoted as the MEANS is not that, and when the item carries a CODE CHECK saying so, DISAGREE (pkgEFG, either side alike). When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. THE FOOTING RULE (pkgECB, ASK 267; either side alike): a LINK BROKEN line whose ground is that the link's step has no footing, or that its footing is borrowed from its own side's contested links, is not a break by meaning, and the meaning test above does not decide it: that the answer's words can agree with the meaning pressed does not answer a missing footing. On such a line a fit that rests on the very step the line says has no footing, or on the answering side's own contested links, is not a fit. AGREE when the answering side's rounds give that step no footing but its own contested links; DISAGREE when you quote the answering side's own words, in the round that gives them, footing the step on rows that are not its own contested links. Footing is the side's own rows and chain, not one verse that states the step (DG-61): a line that only says no verse states the step rests on an absence. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds. CARRIED BY (pkgECW, either side alike): when you DISAGREE with RIGHT: STANDS because the answer's quoted words carry a meaning the link can agree with (a rival reading included), end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", a verse the answering round cites (any layer, the order rows included); or -- CARRIED BY: [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>) at <reference>, a word that verse holds. Without it the STANDS is recorded and not sent back. The CARRIED BY row is never the line's own pressed verse (a verse named at the head of the line, or the GROUND's [L1] verse; for a FORCED line, those of its collision line): that verse holds the words in dispute, and quoting it again shows no rival reading. Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10). A CARRIED BY on the pressed verse is recorded and not sent back (ASK 355). When you AGREE that a link is BROKEN, end that same reply line with -- CARRIED BY: <reference> "<at least 6 words in a row of that verse, as the record holds it>", the row whose words the rival reading cannot also hold (ASK 355, TRIAL: recorded only; the pressed-verse rule does not apply to an AGREE). A DISAGREE that rests on an absence, on THE WITNESS LEDGER, on THE FOOTING RULE, or on a line that quotes no answer words needs no CARRIED BY.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). THE WITNESS LEDGER (pkgWLDDS), when an item gives it, is the system's record of the rounds, the same one the judges were shown: a witness NAMED IN AN ANSWER was answered by name in the round shown, so a line that rests on that witness being unanswered or left unanswered is wrong on that ground (DISAGREE, and say so), though whether that answer meets the meaning pressed is still read from its quoted words; a witness NOT NAMED was named in no later round of the answering side; NAMED ONLY IN OTHER TEXT decides neither. STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. An answer is every line the answering side wrote under the pressed verse, its layers included (THE ANSWER IN FULL, when given under an ANSWER CHECK line); an opening grant followed by a layer that shows the fit is not a bare grant. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not. Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none

}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the answer's own words that fail to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round: its reading, not only the words of a verse it quotes>" -- CARRIED BY: "<the words of the pressed witness's own verse that state its MEANS sentence, quoted from the KJV>" -- GROUND: [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words the answer cannot agree with>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>), when the break turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>", for any cross-reference relied on (Commitment 13). Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. CARRIED BY shows that the pressed verse itself carries the MEANS sentence; K-FC, a TRIAL check, finds its words in that verse as the KJV reads it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures is that Christ had no human biological father, his conception being wrought uniquely by the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary without the agency of human seed or copulation.

### I. Conception by the Holy Ghost Prior to Marital Union

The record of the generation of Jesus Christ opens by defining the temporal and causal origin of the pregnancy:

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

### II. Divine Generation Versus Human Begetting

The Gospel distinguishes between the line of human patrilineal begetting and the divine origin of the child in Mary's womb:

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
